key_insight: POD filtering helps a machine learning surrogate distinguish turbine wakes from background turbulence, reducing prediction error by three orders of magnitude versus training on unfiltered LES data.
engineering_relevance: Fast predictions of mean flow downstream of marine hydrokinetic turbine arrays could support layout optimization in natural waterways with complex bathymetry.
method: Generate instantaneous flow fields using large eddy simulation (LES).
Apply proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) and select modes that preserve wake-relevant structures.
Train a 3D convolutional encoder–decoder to predict time-averaged velocity fields.
evidence_signal: At a real-world tidal river site under ebb tide conditions, the POD-filtered surrogate achieved three orders of magnitude lower mean squared error at equivalent network size and training cost.
watch_item: Transferability to other sites, tidal conditions, and turbine layouts is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: A novel machine learning framework based on proper orthogonal decomposition for turbine wake flow predictions in natural waterways
